tools.name: build_route
tools.description: Returns the review Programscape would show a founder, from what they have said about their company (stage, funding, the tools they use, company type and answers to earlier questions): a short read of what matters at their stage, the programs worth their time now with each one’s standing and the ques

tools.name: my_plan
tools.description: Returns the founder’s saved Programscape plan: their answers, the programs they kept or set aside, and their review as it stands today on those answers. For a returning founder asking where things stand or what to do next.

tools.name: update_my_plan
tools.description: Saves answers and program choices to the founder’s own Programscape plan: new or changed answers, programs to keep, programs to set aside. Creates their first plan if they have none. Only what is sent changes; everything else in the plan (notes, progress, contacts) stays as it is.

tools.name: portfolio_perks
tools.description: If the founder joined a venture firm’s or studio’s perks on Programscape (for example PSL’s), returns that portfolio’s negotiated deals in the partner’s own words, labelled as the partner’s terms, and the public programs the partner points them to, with their live records.

tools.name: partner_perks_admin
tools.description: For the admin of a venture firm’s or studio’s perks list on Programscape (for example PSL’s): what needs a look (deals due to re-confirm, linked programs that changed or closed, imported deals not yet checked), how each perk stands, how many founders joined through each invite link (counts under 3 a

tools.name: save_plan_draft
tools.description: Saves a founder’s review as a one-day draft and returns a link that opens it on programscape.com with their answers and kept programs in place. The founder saves it there with an email code (no password). The link works for 24 hours.

tools.name: profile_questions
tools.description: Returns the shared questions, with their answer options, that shape a founder’s review. A fact the founder hasn’t given stays unknown.

tools.name: search_programs
tools.description: Searches the reviewed catalog of startup credits, programs, support and product discounts across providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, NVIDIA, Stripe and more). Each result carries its official source and the date it was last checked. A listing is not a statement that any

tools.name: get_program
tools.description: Returns one program’s reviewed record: what it offers, who decides, exclusions, official sources and the date checked.

tools.name: compare_programs
tools.description: Returns families of programs that serve the same goal across providers, side by side, with no winner and no score.

tools.name: whats_changed
tools.description: Returns what Programscape’s latest checks against the providers’ own pages found, dated and sourced.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "save_plan_draft" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Saves a founder’s review as a one-day draft and returns a link that opens it on programscape.com with their answers and kept programs in place. The founder save…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: build_route, partner_perks_admin · Private data: update_my_plan, portfolio_perks, save_plan_draft, get_program · Public sink: save_plan_draft.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: build_route, partner_perks_admin · Private data: update_my_plan, portfolio_perks, save_plan_draft, get_program · Public sink: save_plan_draft

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
